Ingest the resolved address crosswalk as historical spells

Source: R/md-ingest-address-crosswalk.R
md_ingest_address_crosswalk.Rd

address_resolved_crosswalk is the NCCS address history: 11,299,800 rows over 3,687,468 EINs, each row one spell an organisation occupied an address, with spell_rank, the vintage range it spans, and how many vintages observed it.

Usage

md_ingest_address_crosswalk(con = NULL, path = NULL, version = "2026-08")

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

path

Path to the crosswalk CSV.

version

Pinned address_crosswalk version.

Value

Row count, invisibly.

Details

It supersedes parsing metadata-addresses, whose ORG_ADDRESS_ALL is a comma-joined string that collides with commas inside street lines (?md_meta_caveats). This file has already done that parse.

Everything here is historical, including spell_rank 0

Every row enters as variant_class = 'historical', and that is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight about rank 0. The crosswalk is an archive of where organisations have been; its most recent spell is not guaranteed to be where they are now, and its last_vintage can be years old. The BMF supplies the current mailing address, and letting a stale spell claim mailing would put a reference to work matching organisations to addresses they have left.

spell_rank and last_vintage are both carried, so a consumer that wants "most recent spell, still current as of a recent vintage" can express it - but has to say so.

Two shape facts worth knowing before selecting this

Street is present on only 61.2% of rows. The remainder carry city, state and ZIP but no street line. Those are still real geography and still block on ZIP, so they are loaded rather than discarded, but a spec that assumes a street on every historical address will be disappointed on four rows in ten.

This roughly triples the address table. It is the largest single source in the database. That is the intended shape - the database holds everything and the spec selects (section 5) - but it makes the section 8 row budget a live concern at compile time rather than a theoretical one.

A parsing hazard, recorded

DuckDB's CSV sniffer mis-detects this file, inferring no quote character, so a street like "849 ALMAR AVE. STE. C, PMB 217" splits into fourteen columns against a thirteen-column header and the read fails. The error text suggests ignore_errors=true, which would silently drop every row containing a comma in its street - precisely the rows most worth having. The fix is to state the quote character rather than let it be guessed.
